title: security(rbac-v2): enforce KMS region residency and expand audit logging for cross-account keys
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: tighten KMS residency guarantees for RBAC v2 resources and improve auditability for operations that use cross-account keys. Customers in regulated regions have requested strict enforcement that KMS keys used for encrypting customer data are resident in the same region as the resource, and security wants richer audit events when KMS key selection falls back to allowlist/denylist logic.

Summary of changes: added enforcement mode for KMS region residency in RBAC v2, extended audit logging to include resolved key meta (key_arn, key_region, key_policy_match), and surfaced enforcement decision reasons in the audit log. Introduced migration path and feature flag (rbac.kms_residency.enforce) to avoid sudden behavior changes.

What I changed (high level):
- RBAC engine: added kms residency enforcement checks and decision enums (ALLOW, AUDIT_ONLY, DENY) with deterministic fallback order.
- API validation: disallow creating RBAC bindings that reference keys outside the allowed region when enforcement is enabled.
- Audit pipeline: emitted structured flat fields for KMS decisions (kms_key_arn, kms_key_region, kms_decision, kms_reason) to existing audit-log topic to make downstream SIEM parsing easier.
- Private installer: added a toggle to enable enforcement at install time and migration job to flag existing bindings that violate residency.
- E2E tests and integration harness: added tests covering enforcement on write, read-only access when audit-only, and migration job reporting.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-1987) linked in PR description
- [x] Unit tests added for decision logic
- [x] Integration tests for audit events and API validation
- [x] Migration job and admin CLI for remediation
- [x] Docs and release notes drafted (internal and public)

Backward compatibility and rollout: enforcement is behind a cluster-level feature flag rbac.kms_residency.enforce (off by default). When enabled, invalid bindings are rejected on create/update. We provide an audit-only mode (rbac.kms_residency.mode = "audit") to surface violations without rejecting requests. The migration job (scripts/migrations/kms_residency_scan.py) will report offending bindings and can optionally remediate by reassigning keys or tagging resources.

Testing and CI: local unit test coverage increased for RBAC decision paths. Integration test suite includes a mocked KMS and runs both audit-only and enforce flows. CI initially showed a flaky integration test (TestKMSRotationPolicy) which was stabilized by increasing mock clock tolerance; all checks pass in latest run.

Monitoring and observability: added metrics rbac.kms_residency.violation_count, rbac.kms_residency.audit_count, and a dashboard tile in Console to list top offending tenants. Audit logs include a flat payload that downstream log processors can index by key_region and decision.

Rollout plan: stage 1 (canary): enable audit-only in staging for 72h and monitor violation_count and customer errors. stage 2: enable audit-only in 10% of production clusters; stage 3: after 2 weeks and zero critical regressions, flip enforcement for targeted compliance customers; stage 4: global enforcement if no major issues.

Related: Linear ENG-1987, SEC-421.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the decision metadata flat in audit logs to avoid nested JSON in existing parsers. Migration script is idempotent and includes a safelist for key ARNs that have explicit exceptions.
